question.text: A water sample has ppm level concentration of following anions,  <math><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>;</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>-</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>;</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>50</mn></math> . The anion/anions that make/makes the water sample unsuitable for drinking is/are

solution.text:
Above 500 ppm of SO42- ions in drinking water, can cause laxative effect otherwise lesser ppm value is permissible for drinking.

Maximum limit of NO3- ions in drinking water is 50 ppm, above this limit it can cause the disease like methemoglobinemia.

More than 1 ppm F- ions in drinking water are not fit for drinking, it can cause decay of bones and teeth.
